full_text_en:
China Environmental Protection Federation v. Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province — dispute over environmental information disclosure

Ruling Summary

Obtaining environmental information in accordance with the law is an important right of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, and is an important means for public participation in environmental protection and supervision of the implementation of environmental laws. A public interest organization with the responsibility of safeguarding the public's environmental rights and interests and social supervision may, in accordance with the law, apply to an environmental protection authority for access to environmental information based on the special needs of other litigation cases. Where the content of the application is clear and specific and the information sought falls within the scope of disclosure, the people's court shall uphold the application.

Plaintiff: China Environmental Protection Federation, domiciled at: East Qingniangou Road, Hepingli District 14, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zeng Xiaodong, Vice Chairman and Secretary-General of the Federation.

Defendant: Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, domiciled at: Renmin South Road, Longchang Town, Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province.

Legal Representative: Zhu Guoxiong, Director of the Bureau.

The China Environmental Protection Federation filed an administrative public interest lawsuit with the Qingzhen City People's Court of Guizhou Province, alleging that the defendant, the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, refused to disclose environmental information.

Plaintiff's Allegations: In October 2011, the plaintiff filed an environmental public interest lawsuit with the Environmental Protection Tribunal of the Qingzhen City People's Court of Guizhou Province, suing Guizhou Haoyiduo Dairy Co., Ltd. for discharging industrial wastewater in excess of standards. Due to the need for relevant environmental information of Haoyiduo in that case, the plaintiff submitted an application to the defendant, the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, requesting the defendant to disclose environmental information concerning Haoyiduo, including the environmental impact assessment report, completion and acceptance documents for pollution control facilities, pollutant discharge permit, and pollutant discharge fee collection. The Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province neither disclosed the above information to the plaintiff within the statutory time limit nor responded to the plaintiff's application, which violated the provisions of the State Council's Regulations on Open Government Information and the Ministry of Environmental Protection's Measures for Environmental Information Disclosure (for Trial Implementation). Therefore, the plaintiff filed an administrative public interest lawsuit with the people's court, requesting a judgment that the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province respond to the plaintiff's application for government information disclosure and disclose the relevant information to the plaintiff.

Defendant's Defense: 1. The plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, did submit an application for government information disclosure by express mail on October 28, 2011, but the application form was not accompanied by the plaintiff's institution code certificate or other identity materials, nor did it specify which of Haoyiduo's three bases the information pertained to; the content of the requested information was unclear. 2. The form in which the plaintiff requested the information was not specific or clear. 3. The plaintiff's method of obtaining the information was unclear. 4. The plaintiff did not provide the relevant costs for retrieval, reproduction, or postage when applying for information disclosure. Moreover, the defendant had informed the plaintiff's contact person, Song Jiebin, by telephone on October 31, 2011, requesting the plaintiff to supplement and clarify the content of the requested information to facilitate the defendant's performance of its duty to disclose information. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim that the defendant failed to perform its statutory duty to disclose government information lacks factual and legal basis.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Qingzhen City People's Court of Guizhou Province):

In October 2011, the plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, filed an environmental public interest lawsuit with the Environmental Protection Tribunal of the Qingzhen City People's Court of Guizhou Province, suing Guizhou Haoyiduo Dairy Co., Ltd. for discharging industrial wastewater in excess of standards. Due to the need for relevant environmental information of Haoyiduo in the case, the plaintiff submitted an application to the defendant, the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, requesting the defendant to disclose environmental information concerning Haoyiduo, including the pollutant discharge permit, the number and locations of discharge outlets, the types and quantities of pollutants discharged, the pollutant discharge fee rate determined by the environmental protection authority, the monitoring results and penalties imposed by the environmental protection authority, the environmental impact assessment documents and approval documents, and the "three simultaneousnesses" acceptance documents. The plaintiff submitted the information disclosure application form to the defendant by notarized mail on October 28, 2011. After receiving the application form, the defendant considered that the content of the information requested by the plaintiff was unclear, the form of the information requested was not specific or clear, and the method of obtaining the information was unclear. Therefore, the defendant did not respond to the plaintiff's application for government information disclosure and did not disclose the requested information to the plaintiff.

The issue in dispute at first instance was whether the information disclosure application submitted by the plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, to the defendant, the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, was clear and specific.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Qingzhen City People's Court of Guizhou Province):

Obtaining environmental information in accordance with the law is an important right of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, and is an important means for public participation in environmental protection and supervision of the implementation of environmental laws. To safeguard this right, relevant laws and regulations provide detailed provisions on the scope, procedures, methods, supervision, and assurance of environmental information disclosure. Environmental information should be disclosed as a principle, with non-disclosure as the exception. The environmental information concerning Haoyiduo requested by the plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, is not prohibited from disclosure by relevant laws and regulations. The defendant's failure to disclose the requested information to the plaintiff violates the provisions of laws and regulations.

The plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, submitted a written application for environmental information disclosure to the defendant, the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, by postal express for the needs of an environmental public interest lawsuit. The application stated the applicant's name, contact information, specific content of the requested disclosure, and method of obtaining the information. The content of the requested environmental information did not involve state secrets, trade secrets, or personal privacy and fell within the scope of government environmental information that may be disclosed by law. The procedure for applying for environmental information also complied with the provisions of Article 20 of the Regulations of the PRC on Open Government Information and Article 16 of the Measures for Environmental Information Disclosure (for Trial Implementation).

Regarding the defendant's argument that the plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, should have attached its identity certificate when submitting the application for government information disclosure: Because the plaintiff had correctly filled in the name of the organization, domicile, contact person, and telephone number in the information disclosure application form and affixed its official seal, and Article 20 of the Regulations of the PRC on Open Government Information clearly stipulates that an application for government information disclosure shall include (1) the name or title and contact information of the applicant; (2) a description of the content of the government information sought to be disclosed; and (3) the form in which the government information is requested. There is no mandatory requirement for the applicant to provide an identity certificate. Therefore, the defendant's argument lacks legal basis.

Regarding the defendant's argument that Haoyiduo has three bases in Xiuwen County and that the plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, did not specify which base's environmental information it was applying for, making the content of the application unclear: According to Article 21 of the Regulations of the PRC on Open Government Information, if the content of an application is unclear, the administrative organ shall inform the applicant to make corrections or supplements. In this case, the plaintiff had clearly stated in the application form that it required the pollutant discharge permit, the number and locations of discharge outlets, the types and quantities of pollutants discharged, the pollutant discharge fee rate determined by the environmental protection authority, the monitoring results and penalties imposed by the environmental protection authority, and the environmental impact assessment documents and approval documents of Guizhou Haoyiduo Dairy Co., Ltd. The expression of the content of the application was clear and specific. The fact that Haoyiduo has several bases in Xiuwen County does not hinder the defendant from disclosing information. The defendant should disclose to the plaintiff all relevant environmental information concerning Haoyiduo in its possession. Additionally, Article 24 of the Interim Provisions of Guizhou Province on Open Government Information stipulates: "An administrative organ shall, in response to an application for disclosure of government information, reply according to the following circumstances: ... (6) if the content of the application is unclear or the formal requirements of the application are incomplete, the administrative organ shall issue a Notice of Correction of Application and inform the applicant to make corrections or supplements in one go." Even if the defendant considered the content of the plaintiff's application unclear, it should have issued a Notice of Correction of Application to the plaintiff in accordance with this provision and informed the applicant to make corrections or supplements in one go. However, the defendant obviously did not handle it in accordance with the regulations. Therefore, the defendant's refusal to disclose information on the grounds that the application content was unclear is not in compliance with the regulations. Furthermore, according to Article 24, Paragraph 2 of the Regulations of the PRC on Open Government Information and Article 18 of the Measures for Environmental Information Disclosure (for Trial Implementation), the defendant clearly failed to perform its obligation to respond within the statutory time limit. Therefore, the defendant's failure to respond to the application violates the provisions of laws and regulations.

Regarding the defendant's argument that the plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, did not provide the relevant costs for retrieval, reproduction, or postage when applying for information disclosure: According to Article 26 of the Interim Provisions of Guizhou Province on Open Government Information, an administrative organ may charge actual costs incurred for retrieval, reproduction, postage, etc. when providing government information upon application. However, the defendant did not request payment from the plaintiff, and the plaintiff did not explicitly indicate that it would not pay the relevant fees. Therefore, the defendant's refusal to disclose environmental information on this ground does not comply with the law.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 13 and Article 26 of the Regulations of the PRC on Open Government Information, Article 16 of the Measures for Environmental Information Disclosure (for Trial Implementation), and Article 1(1) and Article 9, Paragraph 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Administrative Cases Concerning Open Government Information, the Qingzhen City People's Court of Guizhou Province rendered the following judgment on January 10, 2012:

The defendant, the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, respond to the application for government information disclosure of the plaintiff, the China Environmental Protection Federation, and disclose to the plaintiff the relevant environmental information of Guizhou Haoyiduo Dairy Co., Ltd. in accordance with the plaintiff's request.

The Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, refused to accept the judgment of first instance and appealed to the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court of Guizhou Province.

During the proceedings in the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court of Guizhou Province, the appellant, the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, submitted an application for withdrawal of the appeal on March 9, 2012, on the grounds that "the Environmental Protection Bureau's initiative to disclose government information to citizens, legal persons, and other organizations is its duty and responsibility, and it voluntarily submits to the Administrative Judgment (2012) Qing Huan Xing Chu Zi No. 1 of the Qingzhen City People's Court."

Upon review, the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court of Guizhou Province held that the appellant's application for withdrawal of the appeal complied with the law. Pursuant to Article 63, Paragraph 1, Item (10) and Article 97 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, and by reference to Article 156 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered the following ruling on March 12, 2012:

Permission is granted to the appellant, the Environmental Protection Bureau of Xiuwen County, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, to withdraw the appeal.

This ruling is final.
